title: rustc identity memo is keyed on path and size only; a same-size relink reuses the old banner
description:
ResolveRustcFingerprint keys rustc-version-memo-v1 on realpath + size. ResolveCompilerId (C++) adds mtime and its comment explains why: relinking a compiler after a source change routinely lands on the same byte count. Add mtime, bump the memo name to v2. Fails first: a unit test that rewrites the fake rustc with same-size different bytes and a newer mtime and expects a new fingerprint.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Verified facts: `ResolveRustcFingerprint` (src/rust/rust_compile.cc, anonymous namespace) builds the memo key from `"rustc-version-memo-v1"`, `RealPath(rustc)` and `FileSize(real)` only, then reads `<cache>/compilers/<hex>` if present. `ResolveCompilerId` (src/core/compile.cc) uses `"compiler-version-memo-v2"`, path, size **and** `info.mtime`, with the comment explaining why.

| Behaviour | Before | After | Keep? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Same rustc binary, unchanged | memo hit, no `rustc -vV` spawn | memo hit, no spawn | keep: the memo exists to avoid a spawn per crate |
| rustc replaced in place, same size, newer mtime | old banner reused forever, keys collide with the old toolchain's | new memo key, `-vV` re-run, new fingerprint | change (the defect) |
| rustc replaced, different size | new memo | new memo | keep |
| Memo file from v1 present after upgrade | used | ignored (key name changed to `rustc-version-memo-v2`); one extra `-vV` per toolchain, then memoised | change, harmless; old v1 files stay as dead files until `--clear` |
| What travels in the cache key | hash of the banner text | unchanged (mtime is only in the local memo key, never in the cache key) | keep: keys must stay machine-independent so S3 entries share |

Cost: one extra `stat` field already returned by the same `stat` call; zero extra syscalls.

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| `rustc` is a rustup proxy symlink | `RealPath` resolves it first (unchanged); mtime of the resolved file |
| mtime unreadable (stat fails) | same as today when size is unreadable: use 0 and carry on, never fail the compile |
| Two toolchains at different paths, same size and mtime | different memo keys via the path (unchanged) |
| Clock set backwards so the new binary's mtime is older | still a different mtime value, so a different key; the rule is "differs", not "newer" |

Naming: memo key prefix becomes `rustc-version-memo-v2`, mirroring `compiler-version-memo-v2`. No other new names.

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Integration test, new section `9e. Rust: a rustc rebuilt in place is a new toolchain` in tests/integration_test.sh, skipped when `rustc` is absent:
1. Write two fake rustc scripts of byte-identical length under `$WORK/rustc-swap/`: each is `#!/bin/sh` plus a branch that, when `$1` is `-vV`, prints the real `rustc -vV` output with the `release:` line replaced by `release: 9.9.1` (script A) or `release: 9.9.2` (script B); every other invocation `exec`s the real rustc with `"$@"`. Assert `wc -c` of A equals B.
2. Install A as `$WORK/rustc-swap/bin/rustc`; compile the existing `demo` crate through `"$VCACHE" $WORK/rustc-swap/bin/rustc ...` (same flags as section 9). Expect `misses` = 1.
3. Compile again: `hits` = 1 (memo and entry both reused).
4. Copy B over the same path (`cp`, which keeps the size), then `touch -d '+2 seconds'` it so the mtime differs even on coarse filesystems. Compile again: expect `misses` = 2, and `VCACHE_LOG` shows a `rust key` different from step 2's.
Before the fix step 4 shows `hits` = 2 (the stale banner); that is the fail-first evidence.

Mutations to introduce, show failing, revert, and report:
- M1 drop `UpdateU64(mtime)` from the memo key: step 4 hits (fails "a rebuilt rustc misses").
- M2 keep mtime but leave the prefix at `-v1`: the test still passes (old v1 files are per-cache, the test uses a fresh cache) — report as "not caught, by design" with that reason.
- M3 put the mtime into the cache key instead of the memo key: an existing unit/integration check that two checkouts share Rust entries must fail (section 9 "second rust checkout hits" if the scripts are copied with different mtimes; if nothing fails, add that assertion and report it).
close_reason: af21e0b: rustc banner memo includes mtime

title: util::ReadFile reads through istreambuf_iterator: 28% of vcache CPU on a warm build
description:
perf on a warm 357-crate build: ReadFile 28%, BLAKE3 17%, memmove 9% of vcache's own CPU, which is 82% of all CPU in that build; the 550 MB asupersync entry takes 1.7 s to serve. Replace with fstat + a single read into a presized string (or mmap for blobs above a threshold) and remove the extra copies in DeserializeBlob/RestoreOutputs where a string_view suffices. Fails first: none applicable (no behaviour change); record the before/after warm wall time and perf share in the commit body instead.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): behaviour diff

Verified: `util::ReadFile` (src/util/fs.cc) builds a `std::string` from `std::istreambuf_iterator<char>`, byte by byte with reallocations. `DeserializeBlob` (src/storage/chain.cc) then copies the body (`data.substr(pos, body_len)`), BLAKE3-hashes it to check the stored digest, and copies each section payload (`body.substr(bpos, len)`). RestoreOutputs (src/rust/rust_compile.cc) copies each file's contents once more (`std::string contents = file.contents;`) before writing. Measured on a warm 357-crate build: vcache is 82% of all CPU; inside vcache `ReadFile` 28%, BLAKE3 17%, memmove 9%; the 550 MB asupersync entry takes 1.7 s to serve.

| Behaviour | Before | After | Keep? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bytes read for a file | all of it | all of it | keep |
| Missing / unreadable file | `nullopt` | `nullopt` | keep exactly; callers branch on it |
| File that grows or shrinks while read | whatever istreambuf saw | read until EOF after the `fstat` size (loop on short reads, stop at 0); a file that shrank returns the shorter content | keep semantics: return what is there, never pad |
| Blob checksum verification on every Get | yes (BLAKE3 of body) | **yes, unchanged** | keep: it is the integrity check; removing it is out of scope and forbidden |
| Copies of a blob body on a hit | read + body substr + per-section substr + restore copy (4) | read once into a sized buffer; sections parsed as `std::string_view` into the body; contents moved, not copied, into BlobFile; RestoreOutputs writes from a `const std::string&` | change |
| Public signatures | `std::optional<std::string> ReadFile(const std::string&)` | unchanged | keep (many callers) |

New failure modes: none allowed. A `read` that returns EINTR is retried; any other error returns `nullopt` as today.

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| 0-byte file | returns an empty string (not nullopt) |
| /proc-style file whose `st_size` is 0 but has content (`/proc/meminfo`) | returns the content: when `st_size` is 0, fall back to a read loop with a growing buffer |
| FIFO or other non-regular file | same as today (read to EOF) |
| 550 MB blob | one allocation of the final size |
| Truncated blob / bad digest | `DeserializeBlob` false exactly as today |

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): tests, measurement, mutations

Unit tests (Section `util::ReadFile`, new): empty file -> `""`; 3-byte file -> exact bytes; a 64 MiB file of a repeating pattern -> exact size and BLAKE3 equal to `hash::HashFile`; missing path -> nullopt; `/proc/self/status` -> non-empty and starts with `Name:`. Unit (Section `storage::blob`, extend): a blob with two files round-trips byte-exact; flipping one body byte makes `DeserializeBlob` return false.

Measurement in the commit body (not a test): warm build of a cargo workspace through `bin/vcache`, before and after, using the method in the epic (fresh target dir, warm store), wall time and `perf report --comm vcache --sort symbol` top 5. If you cannot run perf, say so; do not invent numbers.

Mutations to report:
- M1 return the content without the final short-read loop (read exactly `st_size` once): the `/proc/self/status` test fails.
- M2 drop the BLAKE3 check in `DeserializeBlob`: the flipped-byte test fails.
- M3 return nullopt for a 0-byte file: the empty-file test fails.
- M4 parse sections with an off-by-one length: the two-file round-trip fails.
- M5 skip `EINTR` retry: report "not caught, by design" (cannot be triggered deterministically) with that reason.

title: Queued S3 upload is skipped when the disk layer evicts the entry first
description:
UploadWorker re-reads the blob from disk; if DiskStorage::Put's inline LRU eviction removed it, the upload is counted as uploads_skipped and lost. Under cache pressure the newest entries are evicted first, so S3 silently loses exactly the latest work. Fix: the evictor skips keys with a pending/<key> journal marker (the journal is already the pin list). Fails first: an integration test with a tiny disk size and a mock S3 showing uploads_skipped stays 0.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Verified: eviction is `DiskStorage::TrimGlobal` (src/storage/disk_storage.cc), called from `DiskStorage::Put` when the cache passes its budget and from `Trim()`. It runs in **every** process that writes the disk layer (each compile without a daemon, and the daemon's `HandlePut`), so a pin must be a filesystem fact, not daemon memory. The daemon's journal is an empty file `<cache dir>/daemon/pending/<key>` (`Server::JournalPath`, `StateDir` = `AbsoluteLexical(disk.dir) + "/daemon"`), created by `Enqueue` when the blob is on disk and removed in `FinishUpload`. `UploadWorker` re-reads the blob from disk at its turn; if eviction removed it, `uploads_skipped++` and the upload is lost.

State of one entry with an S3 layer and a daemon:

| State | Event | Next | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| on disk, journalled | trim selects it | **stays** (skipped, pinned) | VCACHE_LOG `disk: kept <n> entries pending upload` once per trim |
| on disk, journalled | upload done or failed for good | on disk, not journalled | journal file removed (unchanged) |
| on disk, not journalled | trim selects it | evicted (unchanged) | |
| journalled, blob gone (removed outside vcache) | worker turn | skipped (unchanged, counted) | |

Invariant: an entry with a `pending/<key>` file is never removed by TrimGlobal. Bound: pinned bytes can exceed the budget transiently; a trim that cannot reach its target because of pins stops at the pins and logs how many bytes stayed pinned.

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Trim with no daemon dir | evict by LRU | identical (one failed `stat` per candidate only when a `daemon/pending` dir exists: check it once per trim) |
| Trim with pending entries | may evict them | skips them |
| `.linkout` sidecars and other non-key files in shards | evicted by LRU | unchanged (their names are not keys; never pinned) |
| `--clear` | removes everything | unchanged: an explicit clear is the user's call |

Cost: one `stat` of `<dir>/daemon/pending` per trim; when it exists, one `access()` per eviction candidate actually removed.

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| Entry path `<dir>/ab/cdef...` | key = `ab` + `cdef...`; pinned when `<dir>/daemon/pending/abcdef...` exists |
| A pending file for a key whose entry is already gone | ignored |
| Everything pinned | trim removes nothing, logs the pinned count, returns; `Put` still succeeds |
| Read-only cache | no trim (unchanged) |
| Two trimmers at once | unchanged ENOENT accounting; pinned entries counted as kept by both |

Naming: helper `bool DiskStorage::IsPendingUpload(const std::string& entry_path) const`; log marker `disk: kept <n> entries pending upload (<bytes> bytes)`.

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Unit (Section `storage::disk trim`): a DiskStorage with max_size 10 KiB; Put keys k1..k4 of 4 KiB each with lru times oldest k1; create `<dir>/daemon/pending/<k1>`; Put k5 (triggers trim): k1 still present, k2 removed, the total is at or below the high water except for pinned bytes. Without the pending file the same sequence removes k1 (control).
Integration (section `11. Daemon uploads survive eviction`, uses tests/mock_s3.py like the existing S3 sections): daemon on, `VCACHE_CACHE_SIZE` small enough that five compiles overflow it, mock S3 with `MOCK_S3_LATENCY_MS=300` so uploads lag behind stores; after the compiles, `vcache --stop-daemon`; `--daemon-status` taken before stop shows `skipped 0`, and the mock bucket holds all five keys.

Mutations:
- M1 ignore the pending file: unit pinned case fails (k1 evicted).
- M2 derive the key from the file name only (drop the shard prefix): unit fails.
- M3 pin every entry when the pending dir exists: the control part of the unit test (k2 removed) fails.
- M4 skip the pinned check only in the ENOENT branch: report whether caught.
- M5 make an all-pinned trim loop forever: the "everything pinned" unit case must time out the test harness; add an explicit bounded check so it fails, not hangs.
close_reason: 25296ca: trim leaves an entry alone while its upload is pending

title: Server::Enqueue dedupes by key, so a manifest re-Put is absorbed by an in-flight upload of the old value
description:
queued_keys_ makes a second Put of the same key a no-op while the first upload is pending; manifests are mutable, so the newer states never reach S3. Fix: generation-aware enqueue (requeue when the value changed) or re-read the disk value at upload time and loop while it changed. Fails first: a unit test that two Puts of one key with different values end with the second value uploaded.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Verified: `Server::Enqueue` returns true immediately when `queued_keys_` holds the key. `queued_keys_` keeps a key from `Enqueue` until `FinishUpload`, which also covers the time the worker has dequeued the item and is uploading it outside the lock. `UploadWorker` re-reads the disk value at its turn (disk case) or uploads `item.blob` (held case). So a second `Put` of the same key while the first is queued or uploading is absorbed: in the disk case the worker may already have read the old bytes; in the held case `held_` keeps the old blob. Manifests (Rust and dep-scan) are rewritten under one key, so S3 keeps a stale manifest. `FinishUpload` also removes the journal file, so a re-Put's journal is lost.

New state per key: `upload_generation_[key]` (uint64), bumped by every Enqueue of the key; `Upload` carries the generation it was queued or last re-read at.

| State | Event | Next | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| not queued | Enqueue(k) | queued gen=1, journal file created (disk case) | |
| queued gen=g (not yet dequeued) | Enqueue(k) again | queued gen=g+1; held case: held_[k] replaced (held_bytes_ adjusted, capacity check applies to the new size); still one queue entry | |
| in flight at gen=g | Enqueue(k) again | gen=g+1, journal file kept/created | |
| in flight at gen=g, upload done | gen still g | not queued; queued_keys_ erased; journal removed (unchanged) | uploads_done++ |
| in flight at gen=g, upload done | gen now g+1 | **re-queued** with gen=g+1 at the back (disk case re-reads disk; held case uploads held_[k]); journal kept | uploads_done++ (the first upload did happen), VCACHE_LOG `daemon: re-queued <key> (rewritten during upload)` |
| in flight, failed for good | gen changed meanwhile | re-queued as above (the newer value deserves its own attempts) | uploads_failed++ |
| daemon restart | | journal recovery as today; generations start at 1 | |

Invariant: after the last Put of key k returns, the value S3 ends with is that Put's value (or the key is counted failed/skipped), never an earlier one.

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single Put per key (the common case: immutable entries) | one upload | one upload, no extra work |
| Re-Put during queue (held case) | old blob uploaded, new lost | new blob uploaded once |
| Re-Put during upload | new value never uploaded | uploaded after the first finishes |
| held_bytes_ accounting | per first blob | adjusted on replace; never negative |

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| Ten re-Puts of one manifest while one upload is in flight | at most one extra upload after it, carrying the last value |
| Re-Put whose new held blob would exceed kMaxHeldBytes | Enqueue returns false as today (HandlePut then uploads synchronously); the old queued item still uploads the old value, then the generation check re-queues nothing because the synchronous upload already wrote the newest; make sure the generation is not bumped when Enqueue returns false |
| Shutdown with a re-queued item | drained like any queued item |

Naming: `upload_generation_`, `Upload::generation`. Log marker above.

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Unit (Section `daemon::upload generation`; drive `Server`'s queue functions through a test seam or extract the queue into a small class `UploadQueue` in src/daemon/ with Enqueue/Dequeue/Finish and unit-test that — preferred, it keeps the server change small): (a) Enqueue k; Enqueue k with blob B2 before dequeue; dequeue yields B2 once. (b) Enqueue k (disk case); dequeue (gen 1); Enqueue k; Finish(gen 1) re-queues; dequeue yields gen 2; Finish(gen 2) empties. (c) One Put only: exactly one dequeue. (d) Enqueue returning false for size does not bump the generation.
Integration (section `11b`): mock S3 with latency 500 ms; store manifest value V1, then V2 within 100 ms through the daemon; after `--stop-daemon` the mock bucket's object for the key equals V2.

Mutations:
- M1 keep the early `return true` for queued keys: (a) and (b) fail.
- M2 re-queue without bumping the generation (always re-queue): (c) fails (two uploads).
- M3 unlink the journal in FinishUpload even when re-queued: add an assertion in (b) that the journal file exists after Finish(gen 1); it must fail.
- M4 replace held_ without adjusting held_bytes_: assert held_bytes_ after (a); must fail.
- M5 bump generation on a refused Enqueue: (d) fails.

description:

Verified: two manifests are read-modify-written without a lock. title: Daemon as scheduler: single-flight keys, memory-aware admission, jobserver pool
description:
Make the 1.3.0 cache daemon the machine-wide coordinator for every compile and link that goes through vcache: compile a missed key once when several worktrees miss it together (single-flight), start a compile only when the machine can hold it (memory admission), and hand out job slots to ninja, make and cargo from one elastic pool (jobserver mode). Filed upstream as Unto-Labs/vcache#24; this epic is our implementation plan whether or not upstream takes it.

## Why

One 128-core / 125 GB host builds the same C++/Rust monorepo in several git worktrees at once (agents and humans). A `-O3 -ggdb3` C++ TU peaks near 3 GB, a release link above that. Every worktree runs its own `ninja -j N` / `cargo build`, each sized from the memory it saw at *its* start (sunbird's build.sh computes -j from MemAvailable once and says itself that ninja never retunes it), so two or three concurrent builds overcommit, swap, or lose a compiler to the OOM killer. After a shared-header edit every tree also recompiles the same ~400 TUs. vcache is the only process that already knows the key (dedup), could know the cost (admission) and spawns the compiler (realised memory), so the coordination belongs here rather than in a separate daemon that would need all three reported to it.

## What the daemon is today (verified 2026-10-08, dev 2c2c6e0)

A proxy for keys and blobs over a Unix socket: ops kHello, kGet, kPut, kStatus, kShutdown (daemon/protocol.h, kProtocolVersion = 1, unknown versions refused at hello). One connection per request (DaemonClient::RoundTrip closes after each), one thread per connection in Server::Serve, kMaxConnections = 1024, kReplyTimeoutSeconds = 300, Shutdown waits 60 s then shuts leftover fds. Counters are process totals (Server::counters_). held_ buffers blobs awaiting upload only when the disk layer did not take them. It never sees paths, roots, decisions, timings, pids or which tree a key belongs to; every feature here adds that through new ops. Measured on our 357-crate Rust workspace with a disk-only cache: warm 4.2-5.3 s off vs 4.8-5.4 s auto, cold ~115 s either way, raw cargo cold 108 s.

## Ground rules every child keeps

1. Daemon unavailable, refused, VCACHE_DAEMON=off, or the feature's own switch off: behaviour is exactly today's (compile in-process). No feature may turn a daemon failure into a build failure.
2. A lease or reservation is memory-only, dies with its client's socket, is never journalled, and is dropped on daemon restart (waiters are told to proceed locally). Speculative or read-only clients never hold one.
3. A waiting client still occupies a ninja/cargo job slot, so every wait is bounded and logged with its length.
4. kProtocolVersion becomes 2 in .8; an old daemon refuses at hello and the client falls back (rule 1).
5. One held connection per in-flight compile (a CompileSession, .8) carries lease, reservation and spawned-pid messages; RoundTrip's per-request connections stay for Get/Put. Shutdown closes sessions immediately instead of waiting on them; Idle() counts an open session as a client.
6. Every integration test asserts on VCACHE_LOG lines and --daemon-status rows, not only on exit codes, so a regression says which decision went wrong.

## Naming (bead ids cannot be renamed)

| concept | name | why |
|---|---|---|
| per-compile held connection | CompileSession (server), DaemonClient::OpenCompileSession, Op::kSessionOpen | joins Upload/UploadWorker naming; "session" alone fails out-of-context |
| single-flight hold on a key | KeyLease, Server::leases_ | the key is what is leased |
| ops | Op::kLeaseAcquire, kLeaseRelease, kMemoryReserve, kCompilerSpawned | join the Op enum; noun-verb states the purpose |
| memory grant | MemoryReservation, Server::reservations_ | |
| cost record | CompileCost {max_rss_kb, wall_ms, recorded_at}, CostKey, dir <cache>/costs/ | sibling of <cache>/compilers/ memos |
| ProcResult additions | max_rss_kb, wall_ms | units in the name |
| config | daemon.single_flight, daemon.admission, daemon.default_compile_kb, daemon.default_link_kb, daemon.jobserver, daemon.jobserver_jobs | join the [daemon] table; env VCACHE_DAEMON_<KEY> |
| CLI | --show-costs, --jobserver-env | join --show-stats / --daemon-status |
| counters (--daemon-status rows) | leases held / waiting / expired, compiles deduplicated; memory reserved_kb / realised_kb / reserve waits; jobserver tokens total / free / withdrawn | |
| log markers (VCACHE_LOG) | "lease: ", "reserve: ", "jobserver: ", "cost: " | one topic word, like "rust manifest: " |
| fifo | <state dir>/jobserver.fifo | beside sock, lock, pending/ |

## Workflow for every child

Branch feat/<slug> from origin/main (our integration branch: upstream 1.3.0 + fork fixes; baseline make test 499 unit / 379 integration checks, 0 failed). export MAKEFLAGS=-j8 and keep /usr/lib64/ccache off PATH. Every new check is shown failing first and recorded as `Fails first:` in the commit body (AGENTS.md). Push the branch, merge --no-ff into main, push main:main. Commits that change the binary end with `Deploy: vcache`; rebuild dist/ with devtools' host-setup-buildcache.sh --force after the merge. Update docs/daemon.md and docs/configuration.md in the same commit as the feature. Do not touch the sibling repos' vcache-env.sh from these beads; .5 files those follow-ups.

## Order

.1 cost records and .8 compile sessions first (both small; admission reads .1, and .2/.3 sit on .8). .2 single-flight and .3 admission are then independent of each other. .4 fixed jobserver pool is independent too. .7 elastic pool needs .3 and .4. .5 build-tool integration needs .4 (and .7 for the elastic claim). .6 measurement last.

title: Cost records: wait4 peak RSS and wall time in blob meta, <cache>/costs/, and --show-costs
description:
## What

util::Run (src/util/subprocess.cc) waits with waitpid and throws resource usage away. Switch to wait4 and add to ProcResult: `uint64_t max_rss_kb` (ru_maxrss) and `uint64_t wall_ms` (monotonic clock around fork..wait). For the clang/gcc driver, wait4's ru_maxrss is the peak of the largest waited-for child, i.e. cc1plus/cc1, which is the number that matters; rustc is single-process; a link is the linker itself. Nothing else about Run changes.

Record the two numbers for every compile and link that vcache runs on a miss (RunCompile, RunRustCompile, RunLink; not dep-info or -E probes):
1. In the blob's meta string on store, as lines `max_rss_kb: N` and `wall_ms: N` after the existing `rustc:`/`crate:`/`roots:` lines (meta is informational and not part of any key, so no key bump).
2. In a CompileCost record under `<cache>/costs/<CostKey hex>`: a small text file with the last 8 observations (`max_rss_kb wall_ms recorded_at_unix`), written by the client with WriteFileAtomic (a lost race drops one observation, acceptable). CostKey = BLAKE3 of (operation: compile|rustc|link, canonical source path or link output path, language, codegen flag class). The flag class is the key_args with -I/-D/-include/paths removed, i.e. the optimisation and debug flags, so a miss on new content of the same file still has an estimate. Content is deliberately not in it.
3. `vcache --show-costs` prints per operation: records, p50 and max of max_rss_kb and wall_ms, and the 10 largest cost keys with their source path.

Estimate lookup (used by .3): max of the recorded max_rss_kb for the cost key; absent, the config default for the operation.

## Logging

VCACHE_LOG gets one line per recorded compile: `cost: <op> max_rss_kb=<n> wall_ms=<n> key=<costkey[0:16]> <source>`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (tests/unit_test.cc, new Section "core::cost"): CostKey ignores content and roots but changes with the flag class and the operation; a CompileCost file round-trips and keeps only the last 8; the estimate is the max, not the mean.
- Unit: util::Run on a child that allocates 64 MB reports max_rss_kb >= 65536 and wall_ms within the measured bound.
- Integration (new section "9d. Cost records"): a compile's blob meta carries `max_rss_kb:` > 0; `--show-costs` lists the compile; `VCACHE_LOG` has the `cost:` line.

## Docs

docs/configuration.md: `--show-costs`; docs/design.md: what meta carries. Commit ends `Deploy: vcache`.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Verified: `util::Run` (src/util/subprocess.cc) forks, pumps the pipes, then `waitpid(pid, &status, 0)` in an EINTR loop; `ProcResult` has exit_code, signalled, stdout_data, stderr_data. Callers of interest: `RunCompile` (src/core/compile.cc, the compile on a miss), `RunRustCompile` (src/rust/rust_compile.cc, the `rust compile:` run), `RunLink` (src/core/link.cc). Probes that must NOT be recorded: `-E`, dep-scan, dep-info, `-v`/`-vV`, passthroughs.

Long-lived state: `<cache>/costs/<CostKey hex>`, one file per cost key, the last 8 observations.

| State | Event | Next |
|---|---|---|
| no file | recorded compile | file with 1 line |
| n < 8 lines | recorded compile | n+1 lines, newest last |
| 8 lines | recorded compile | oldest dropped |
| any | two processes record at once | last WriteFileAtomic wins; one observation may be lost (accepted) |
| any | `--clear` | kept: `DiskStorage::Clear` removes only the 256 shards, and leaves `compilers/` the same way; costs survive a clear like the compiler memos |
| corrupt file | read | treated as empty and rewritten on the next record |

| Behaviour | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Run's exit code / signal reporting | waitpid status | identical, via wait4 status |
| Blob meta | existing lines | existing lines + `max_rss_kb: N` + `wall_ms: N` (meta is in no key; verify by grep that no key hashes meta) |
| Cache keys | | unchanged; no version bump |
| Extra I/O per miss | none | one small file read and one atomic write under costs/ |
| Hit path | | untouched (nothing recorded on a hit) |

New failure modes: a failure to write the cost file must never fail or slow the compile beyond the write attempt; log `cost: could not record (<why>)` and carry on.

## For-Grok pass 2 (2026-10-08): operational cases

| Input | Required behaviour |
|---|---|
| Compiler killed by a signal | still recorded (the peak matters most for OOM kills), with exit noted in the log line |
| Compile failed (exit 1) | recorded |
| wait4 unavailable (macOS has it; any POSIX has it) | no fallback needed; build fails at compile time if missing |
| ru_maxrss units | Linux KiB; macOS bytes: convert so `max_rss_kb` is KiB on both (`#ifdef __APPLE__` divide by 1024) |
| Link with `-flto` spawning lld plus LTO jobs | ru_maxrss is the largest waited-for child; record it as is and say so in docs |
| Cost key flag class | key_args minus `-I*`, `-isystem`, `-D*`, `-U*`, `-include`, `-o`, path-like args canonicalised away; keep `-O*`, `-g*`, `-march=*`, `-f*`, `--edition`, `-C opt-level`, `-C debuginfo` and the language |

Naming: `ProcResult::max_rss_kb`, `ProcResult::wall_ms`, `struct CompileCost`, `std::string ComputeCostKey(...)`, files `src/core/cost.{h,cc}`, dir `<cache>/costs/`, CLI `--show-costs`, log marker `cost: `.

## For-Grok pass 3 (2026-10-08): exact tests and mutations

Unit (Section `util::Run rusage`): add a tiny C++ helper built by the Makefile's test target (`bin/vcache_test_alloc <MiB>`: malloc, memset every page, exit 0) and run it through util::Run; assert max_rss_kb >= 65536 for 64 and < 65536 for 1; wall_ms >= 0 and below 10 000.
Unit (Section `core::cost`): ComputeCostKey equal for two sources with different contents and different roots mapping to the same canonical path; differs for `-O2` vs `-O3`, for compile vs link, for C vs C++; CompileCost round-trip keeps the last 8 in order; estimate = max; a corrupt file reads as empty.
Integration (section `9d. Cost records`): one C++ compile miss: the stored blob's meta contains `max_rss_kb:` > 0 (there is no CLI to dump an entry: find the entry file under the shard for the key logged in VCACHE_LOG and grep it with `grep -a`, meta is stored as plain text inside the blob); `--show-costs` prints a `compile` row with records 1; VCACHE_LOG has exactly one `cost: compile` line; a second (hit) run adds no `cost:` line.

Mutations: M1 keep waitpid (max_rss_kb 0): rusage unit fails; M2 record on hits too: integration "no cost line on hit" fails; M3 put content into the cost key: unit "different contents equal" fails; M4 keep 9 observations: round-trip fails; M5 estimate = last instead of max: estimate unit fails; M6 record dep-info runs: integration expects exactly one cost line; fails.

title: Single-flight: KeyLease over a CompileSession so concurrent worktrees compile a missed key once
description:
## What Several worktrees that miss on one key compile it once. docs/design.md chose duplicate compiles deliberately for a single build, where a lock costs more than the duplicate; across worktrees the duplicate is real (a shared-header edit makes every tree recompile the same ~400 TUs). Switch: `daemon.single_flight = true` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_SINGLE_FLIGHT), default off until .6 has measured it. ## Protocol On the CompileSession from .8 (opened once the key is computed, closed after the outputs are restored or the compile has failed): - `kLeaseAcquire(key, bound_ms)` -> kOk + u8 outcome: `granted` (the session now holds the KeyLease), `stored` (the holder's kPut landed while we waited; do an ordinary kGet), or `compile` (holder failed or vanished, or bound reached). The daemon holds the reply for the waiter until one of those happens; the bound is the client's, computed from the holder's recorded wall_ms (from .1) that the first, immediate reply carries when the key is held: the client sends kLeaseAcquire once with bound_ms=0 to learn the holder's wall_ms, then once more with its bound. - `kLeaseRelease(key, outcome: stored|failed)` from the holder. HandlePut of that key also releases and wakes waiters. - A waiter's wait ends on: the holder's kPut (outcome stored), the holder's release with `failed` (compile), the holder's session closing without a release (compile), daemon shutdown (compile), or the bound (compile). - Bound: max(2 x holder wall_ms, 30 s), capped at kReplyTimeoutSeconds. A waiting wrapper still occupies a ninja/cargo job slot, so no unbounded wait. - Leases are memory-only, never journalled; a daemon restart drops them and reconnecting waiters are told to compile. A speculative or read-only (VCACHE_READONLY) client never acquires. - Concurrent S3 GETs of one key coalesce through the same table: the first Get of a missing-on-disk key fetches, later Gets of it wait for that fetch. ## Server KeyLease {key, holder session, acquired_at, holder_wall_ms, waiters}; Server::leases_ beside queued_keys_. A waiter's session thread blocks on the lease's condition variable with the bound as its timeout (one thread per connection, as today), never on a kGet. Session lifetime, shutdown and Idle() rules come from .8. Counters: leases held, leases waiting, leases expired, compiles deduplicated; --daemon-status rows for all four. ## Client RunCompile, RunRustCompile and RunLink call acquire between key computation and the compile and release after store/failure. Waiters log every transition. ## Logging `lease: acquired `, `lease: waiting on holder pid

up to ms`, `lease: holder stored, serving hit after ms`, `lease: holder failed, compiling`, `lease: holder gone, compiling`, `lease: wait bound reached, compiling`, `lease: released `. ## Tests (fail first) - Unit (new Section "daemon::lease"): grant/deny per key; holder session close expires the lease and wakes waiters with "compile"; failed outcome wakes with "compile"; a stored outcome wakes with "get"; the wait bound arithmetic. - Integration (new section "10b. Single-flight"): two trees, same key, a fake compiler that sleeps 2 s and counts runs through a shared file, VCACHE_DAEMON=auto: exactly one `rust compile:`/`compile:` log line across both VCACHE_LOGs, one `lease: acquired` and one `lease: holder stored`, both trees' outputs byte-identical, `compiles deduplicated 1` in --daemon-status. A second run kills the holder (fake compiler exits 1): the waiter logs `lease: holder failed, compiling` and both trees finish. A third with the daemon stopped mid-wait: `lease: holder gone, compiling`. ## Docs docs/daemon.md: a "Single-flight" section with the rules above and the measured dedup count placeholder filled by .6. `Deploy: vcache`. ## For-Grok pass 1-3 (2026-10-08): state, cases, oracle (routed to Sol; tables still binding) KeyLease state per key: | State | Event | Next | Reply to waiters | |---|---|---|---| | free | A: kLeaseAcquire(k) | held by A | A: granted | | held by A | B: kLeaseAcquire(k, 0) | held, B learns holder_wall_ms | B: immediate `held` reply with wall_ms | | held by A | B: kLeaseAcquire(k, bound) | B waits | | | held by A | A: kPut(k) (any connection) | free | all waiters: stored | | held by A | A: kLeaseRelease(k, failed) | free | all waiters: compile | | held by A | A's session closes without release or put | free, expired++ | all waiters: compile | | held by A | B's bound passes | held by A | B: compile (B then compiles unleased) | | held by A | daemon Shutdown | gone | all waiters: compile | | held by A | A: kLeaseAcquire(k) again | held by A (idempotent) | A: granted | | any | B's session closes while waiting | B removed from waiters | | Same-turn interleavings to test explicitly (the class Grok missed elsewhere; Sol must also cover them): A's kPut and A's session close arriving together (stored must win: waiters get `stored`, not `compile`); B's bound expiring in the same tick as A's kPut (either answer is acceptable but the waiter must not get two replies); A's kLeaseRelease(stored) then kPut (release first: waiters told `stored`, then the Get must hit — if the Put has not landed yet the waiter's Get misses and it compiles, which is safe; document it). Invariants: a key never has two holders; every waiter gets exactly one reply; a holder that dies wakes all its waiters within one second; with single_flight off no lease op is ever sent. Operational cases: holder compile fails (exit 1) -> release failed; holder's store fails (disk full) -> release failed, waiters compile; read-only client never acquires; the dep-info/manifest Put of a Rust crate uses the manifest key, not the entry key: lease only the entry key, never manifest keys; links lease their pre-key/link key the same way. Mutations: M1 grant two holders; M2 wake waiters with `compile` on kPut; M3 no expiry on session close (waiter hangs to its bound: the test bound is 3 s and asserts the holder-gone path answers in under 1.5 s); M4 lease manifest keys; M5 drop the bound (waiter waits forever) — each must fail a named test. ## Reviewer decision (2026-10-08): lease wait bound, answers Sol's stop on vcache-cug.2 Correct stop: the specified fields cannot carry the holder's recorded wall_ms. Decision, superseding the two-step kLeaseAcquire text in the Protocol section and pass 1-3: 1. **No protocol field for cost.** `kLeaseAcquire(key, bound_ms)` is a single request; there is no bound_ms=0 query and no holder wall_ms in any reply. Outcomes unchanged: `granted` | `stored` | `compile`. 2. **The waiter computes its own bound.** Same entry key implies the same canonical source and codegen flags, so the waiter's own CostKey equals the holder's. Bound = max(2 x recorded wall_ms, 30 s), capped at kReplyTimeoutSeconds, where recorded wall_ms is the max over the waiter's own `/costs/` record. No record: 30 s. 3. **Do not wait for vcache-cug.1.** Implement the bound as a pure function, e.g. `uint64_t LeaseWaitBoundMs(std::optional recorded_wall_ms)`, unit-tested on (none -> 30 000; 5 000 -> 30 000; 20 000 -> 40 000; huge -> cap). Call it with `std::nullopt` for now. When vcache-cug.1 is on origin/main (Grok is fixing review findings; the reviewer will tell you), wire in the cost lookup as a one-line change in your vcache-cug.3 work and note it in .3's report. 4. The bead's dependency edge on vcache-cug.1 stays; it is satisfied by 3 for now. 5. Your cug.8 follow-up commit: approved as reported in the pane (519 unit / 426 integration). Push it on your branch if not already, and list R3 "not caught" with its reason in the .2 report.

title: Memory admission: kMemoryReserve against MemAvailable minus unrealised in-flight reservations
description:
## What

Start a compile or link only when the machine can hold it. Switch: `daemon.admission = true` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_ADMISSION), default off until .6 has measured it. Replaces each build's start-of-build `-j` guess with one machine-wide view across worktrees.

## Protocol (on the CompileSession from .8)

- `kMemoryReserve(cost_key, estimate_kb, bound_ms)` -> kOk + u8 outcome `granted` | `bound` (proceed unreserved after bound_ms, logged) + u64 waited_ms. The daemon holds the reply while the client waits; the session is dedicated, so holding it blocks nothing else. bound_ms defaults to 10 minutes.
- `kCompilerSpawned(pid)` right after util::Run forks, so the daemon can sample that pid.
- The reservation ends when the session closes (compile done or client gone).

## Admission arithmetic (server)

available_kb = MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo (re-read at most once a second) minus unrealised_kb, where unrealised_kb = sum over in-flight reservations of max(0, estimate_kb - rss_kb(pid)), rss_kb sampled from /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS every 500 ms (0 until kCompilerSpawned). A resident compile is thereby not counted twice against MemAvailable. Grant when available_kb >= estimate_kb. FIFO queue of waiters, granted in order as reservations end or sampled RSS grows. Always at least one reservation in flight: an estimate larger than the machine is granted when nothing else holds one, so nothing deadlocks. Estimate = .1's cost table for the cost key, else daemon.default_compile_kb (default 2097152) / daemon.default_link_kb (default 4194304). v1 may skip RSS sampling and treat the whole estimate as unrealised for its first 10 s; the test seam below must then be respected by both forms.

Test seam: env VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO=<path> makes the daemon read that file instead of /proc/meminfo (undocumented outside tests, like the existing memo paths).

## Counters / status

reserved_kb, realised_kb, reserve waits, longest wait ms; --daemon-status rows "memory reserved / realised / waiting".

## Client

Reserve in RunCompile, RunRustCompile, RunLink after the key (and after a granted lease, if .2 is on: a lease waiter holds no memory) and before the compile; the dep-info and -E runs are not reserved (small). On any daemon error: proceed unreserved and log it (ground rule 1).

## Logging

`reserve: granted <kb> kB after <ms> ms (available <kb>, unrealised <kb>)`, `reserve: waiting (<available> < <estimate>) behind <n>`, `reserve: daemon unavailable, running unreserved`, server log `reserve: <pid> rss <kb> of <estimate>`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (new Section "daemon::admission"): grant, refuse, FIFO order, the always-one rule, release on session close, realised RSS reducing the unrealised sum, and the cost-table-else-default estimate.
- Integration (new section "10c. Memory admission"): VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO points at a file with MemAvailable 3 GB, two compiles with 2 GB estimates (seeded cost files): the second logs `reserve: waiting` and is granted only after the first's `lease`/session ends; --daemon-status shows `reserve waits 1`; with the daemon stopped both run unreserved and log it.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md "Memory admission" with the arithmetic and defaults; docs/configuration.md for the keys. `Deploy: vcache`.

## For-Grok pass 1-3 (2026-10-08): state, cases, oracle (routed to Sol; tables still binding)

MemoryReservation states:

| State | Event | Next |
|---|---|---|
| none | kMemoryReserve(est) and available >= est, or nothing else reserved | granted (reservations_ += est, rss 0) |
| none | otherwise | queued (FIFO) |
| queued | reservations end / RSS grows / MemAvailable rises so head fits | granted (strict FIFO: a later small request never jumps the head) |
| queued | bound passes | outcome `bound`, client runs unreserved |
| granted | kCompilerSpawned(pid) | sampling that pid every 500 ms |
| granted | pid exits / session closes | released; queue re-evaluated at once |
| granted | sampled RSS > estimate | unrealised 0 for it (never negative); record the overshoot in the daemon log |
| any | daemon restart | all gone; clients see their session end and proceed unreserved |

Same-turn interleavings: a release and a new reserve in the same tick (the release must be applied first); MemAvailable read stale by up to 1 s while three grants happen (the unrealised sum, not MemAvailable, carries the in-flight cost, so this is safe: test three back-to-back reserves against a fake meminfo of 5 GB with 2 GB estimates: grant, grant, queue).

Operational cases: estimate 0 or missing cost record -> default per operation; a link's estimate larger than total RAM -> granted only when alone; /proc/<pid> vanished between samples -> treat as released only on session close, not on a failed read; container clients (pid namespace): SO_PEERCRED gives the daemon-side pid and the client-reported pid may differ: sample the pid the client reports only if it is visible in /proc and its ppid matches the SO_PEERCRED pid; otherwise fall back to the "whole estimate unrealised for 10 s" rule for that reservation and log it.
Mutations: M1 FIFO jump by a small request; M2 count realised RSS against both MemAvailable and unrealised (double count: the three-reserve test queues the second); M3 drop the always-one rule (an over-RAM estimate deadlocks: test with a 1 GB fake meminfo and a 2 GB estimate must grant); M4 release on a failed /proc read; M5 ignore the bound — each must fail a named test.

title: Jobserver mode: a fixed fifo job-slot pool that ninja, make and cargo draw from
description:
## What

The daemon owns one GNU-make-style fifo job-slot pool for every build on the machine. Verified locally: ninja 1.13.2 follows `MAKEFLAGS=--jobserver-auth=fifo:PATH` when no -j is given on its command line (POSIX fifo form only; -l load limits still apply); GNU make 4.4.1 implements the fifo protocol; cargo 1.97 and rustc use the jobserver crate (.5 verifies the fifo form with strace before any sibling repo relies on it). This bead is the fixed-size pool; .7 makes it elastic.

## Behaviour

- `daemon.jobserver = true` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER) and `daemon.jobserver_jobs = N` (env VCACHE_DAEMON_JOBSERVER_JOBS, default: online CPUs). On start the daemon creates `<state dir>/jobserver.fifo` (mkfifo 0600, same ownership rules as the socket) and writes N tokens ('+' bytes, as make does). It keeps a read-write fd open so the fifo never sees EOF.
- `vcache --jobserver-env` prints `MAKEFLAGS=-j --jobserver-auth=fifo:<path>` (and nothing else, exit 1 when no daemon or jobserver is running) for a build script to export. The `-j` with no count is what tells make it is a jobserver client.
- --stop-daemon removes the fifo; --daemon-status shows `jobserver tokens total / free / withdrawn` (withdrawn is 0 until .7).
- A build started with the MAKEFLAGS but no daemon falls back to the tools' own defaults (ninja warns and uses its default -j; document that).

## Logging

`jobserver: pool <path> with <N> tokens`, `jobserver: removed <path>`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (Section "daemon::jobserver"): fifo creation and removal, token count written, --jobserver-env output format.
- Integration (new section "10d. Jobserver"): with the daemon started with jobserver_jobs=2, a Makefile of 6 targets whose recipe is a fake compiler that sleeps 1 s and records its concurrent peers in a shared counter file; `make` under the exported MAKEFLAGS never records more than 2 peers; the same with a tiny build.ninja and `ninja` (no -j). Without the daemon the same make runs 6 wide.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md "Jobserver mode" with the version requirements and the exported line; docs/configuration.md keys. `Deploy: vcache`.

## For-Grok pass 1 (2026-10-08): state and behaviour diff

Long-lived state: the fifo `<state dir>/jobserver.fifo` and its N tokens, owned by the daemon process.

| State | Event | Next | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| daemon not running | `--start-daemon` with daemon.jobserver | fifo created 0600 (mkfifo), daemon opens it O_RDWR (never sees EOF) and writes N '+' bytes | log `jobserver: pool <path> with <N> tokens` |
| running | client reads a token | N-1 in fifo (client holds one) | |
| running | client writes it back | N | |
| running | client crashes holding a token | token lost until daemon restart (same as make); documented, not fixed in this bead | |
| running | `--stop-daemon` / idle exit | fifo removed after the listen socket closes | log `jobserver: removed <path>` |
| a stale fifo from a crashed daemon | next start | recreated (remove the stale path first; it is ours by construction: in our state dir, a fifo) | |
| daemon.jobserver false | start | no fifo (unchanged behaviour) | |

Idle exit: a build blocked reading the fifo is not a socket client; the daemon must not exit idle while tokens are out (fifo bytes < N, check with FIONREAD on the daemon's fd) — keep it running until all tokens are back or the idle timeout passes twice.

| Behaviour | Before | After |

title: Elastic jobserver pool: withdraw free tokens under memory pressure, restore when it clears
description:
## What

Make the jobserver pool from .4 elastic under memory pressure, using the admission view from .3. A token sitting in the fifo is a slot nobody is using, so the daemon can shrink the pool by reading free tokens back out and grow it by writing them back; a token held by a running job is never touched (the job returns it itself).

## Policy v1

Every 500 ms (the same tick that samples RSS): if there are reservations waiting in the admission queue, withdraw min(free tokens, waiting reservations) tokens; when the queue is empty and available_kb exceeds the largest default estimate, restore withdrawn tokens one per tick. Never withdraw below `daemon.jobserver_min_jobs` (default 2). The policy is one function over (free, withdrawn, waiting, available_kb) so it can be unit-tested and replaced.

## Counters / status

jobserver tokens withdrawn (now live), tokens restored total; --daemon-status shows them.

## Logging

`jobserver: withdrew <n> tokens (waiting <n>, available <kb> kB)`, `jobserver: restored <n> tokens`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit: the policy function on a table of (free, withdrawn, waiting, available) -> action rows, including the minimum floor and the one-per-tick restore.
- Integration (extends "10d"): jobserver_jobs=4, VCACHE_DAEMON_MEMINFO at 3 GB, fake compiles with 2 GB estimates under make: the peer counter never exceeds 2 while reservations wait, and returns to 4 after they drain; both `jobserver: withdrew` and `jobserver: restored` appear in the daemon log.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md: the elastic policy and its floor. `Deploy: vcache`.

## For-Grok pass 1-3 (2026-10-08): state, cases, oracle (routed to Sol; tables still binding)

Pool state: total N (config), free F (FIONREAD on the daemon fd), withdrawn W (held by the daemon, not in the fifo), in use U = N - F - W.

| Event (per 500 ms tick) | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| reservations waiting Q > 0 | F > 0 and N - W > jobserver_min_jobs | read min(F, Q, N - W - min_jobs) tokens out of the fifo (non-blocking read on the daemon's fd); W += that |
| Q = 0 | W > 0 and available_kb > max(default_compile_kb, default_link_kb) | write 1 token back; W -= 1 |
| daemon stop | W > 0 | write W back before removing the fifo (clients mid-read must not hang on a fifo that loses tokens) |

Invariants: W never exceeds N - min_jobs; tokens in use are never touched (only free tokens are read); after all reservations drain and memory recovers, W returns to 0 within W ticks.
Operational cases: a client reads the last free token in the same tick the daemon tries to withdraw (the non-blocking read returns EAGAIN: no withdraw, retry next tick); min_jobs > N (clamp to N, warn); jobserver on but admission off (no Q signal: the pool stays fixed; say so in docs).
Mutations: M1 withdraw below min_jobs; M2 blocking read on withdraw (daemon tick stalls: a test with F = 0 must still tick within 1 s); M3 restore all at once; M4 forget to return W on stop (a client blocked in read hangs: test with a 2 s timeout); M5 withdraw when admission is off — each must fail a named test.

title: CompileSession: one held connection per in-flight compile, protocol version 2
description:
## What

The shared scaffolding that single-flight (.2) and memory admission (.3) both build on, landed once so neither has to guess which comes first: a CompileSession, i.e. one held connection per in-flight compile, and protocol version 2.

## Protocol

- kProtocolVersion 1 -> 2. An old daemon refuses a v2 client at hello and the client falls back in-process; a v1 client is refused by a v2 daemon the same way (today's rule, unchanged).
- New op `Op::kSessionOpen` (after kHello on a fresh connection): marks the connection as a CompileSession. Reply kOk. Later ops on it (added by .2 and .3) may have their reply held by the daemon while the client waits; every held reply has a client-side bound and the daemon never holds a reply on a non-session connection.
- The session ends when the client closes the socket (outputs restored, compile failed, or the client died). Everything a session holds (added by .2 and .3) is released then.
- DaemonClient::OpenCompileSession(config) returns a session object whose destructor closes it; RoundTrip's one-connection-per-request behaviour is unchanged for Get/Put.

## Server

Sessions are tracked in Server::sessions_ (fd, client pid from SO_PEERCRED, opened_at). Shutdown closes sessions immediately with Status::kError "daemon shutting down" instead of waiting on them; Idle() counts an open session as a client; kMaxConnections = 1024 still bounds sessions plus requests, which covers -j-many compiles. Counter: sessions open; --daemon-status row "compile sessions N".

## Client

RunCompile, RunRustCompile and RunLink open a session only when daemon.single_flight or daemon.admission is on (both off: no session, no new connection, so a daemon-off or unaware build is byte-for-byte today's). On any session error the compile proceeds as if there were no daemon and logs `session: daemon unavailable (<why>), continuing`.

## Logging

`session: opened`, `session: closed after <ms> ms`, `session: daemon unavailable (<why>), continuing`.

## Tests (fail first)

- Unit (Section "daemon::session"): a v1 hello is refused by a v2 daemon with the version named; a session survives a request on another connection; closing the fd ends the session; Shutdown with an open session returns without waiting the 60 s.
- Integration (new section "10a. Compile sessions"): with daemon.single_flight on and a running daemon, one compile logs `session: opened` and `session: closed`; with the daemon stopped mid-compile the compile still finishes and logs `session: daemon unavailable`; `compile sessions 0` in --daemon-status after the run.

## Docs

docs/daemon.md: a "Compile sessions" paragraph under the protocol description. `Deploy: vcache`.

## For-Grok pass 1-3 (2026-10-08): state, cases, oracle (routed to Sol; tables still binding)

State of one CompileSession:

| State | Event | Next | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | client opens socket, kHello v2 ok, kSessionOpen | open (sessions_ has fd, pid via SO_PEERCRED, opened_at) | client log `session: opened` |
| open | client closes fd | closed; everything it holds released (leases, reservations, added later) | daemon log line; client `session: closed after <ms> ms` |
| open | client process killed | same as close (the kernel closes the fd); the session thread sees EOF/ECONNRESET | |
| open | daemon Shutdown | daemon sends kError "daemon shutting down" if a reply is pending, closes fd; does not wait 60 s for it | client proceeds in-process, logs `session: daemon unavailable (daemon shutting down), continuing` |
| open | idle timer | Idle() returns false while any session is open | |
| none | v1 client hello to v2 daemon | refused, reason names both versions | client falls back (unchanged rule) |
| none | daemon absent / refused | no session; compile proceeds | `session: daemon unavailable (<why>), continuing` once per compile |

Operational cases: `-j128` worktree build = up to 128 sessions plus requests, below kMaxConnections = 1024 (state it in docs); a client that opens a session then never sends anything holds one thread until it closes (no timeout in this bead: a compile can legitimately take an hour); two sessions from one pid (link and compile in one process? vcache is one process per invocation, so at most one; assert it).
Mutations: M1 keep kProtocolVersion 1: the v1-refused unit test fails; M2 Shutdown waits on sessions: the "Shutdown returns promptly" test fails (bound it at 2 s); M3 Idle() ignores sessions: a test that holds a session over a 1 s idle timeout and expects the daemon alive fails; M4 open a session when both switches are off: the integration test asserting no `session:` line with both off fails; M5 leave the fd in sessions_ after close: `compile sessions 0` assertion fails.
acceptance_criteria: kProtocolVersion == 2; unit Section daemon::session (v1 refused, session survives other requests, fd close ends it, Shutdown does not wait); integration 10a logs session: opened/closed and daemon-unavailable fallback; compile sessions row in --daemon-status; Fails first recorded; Deploy: vcache
